notes:
Lead: Lanebreaker builds an embedded product assistant for PMs — wants predictable latency for in-app chat + semantic search. Eng lead (Ishani) ran hosted trial Jan 15–Feb 2.

Trial highlights and metrics (hosted API):
- Primary workloads: in-app chat (conversational UI), doc search/reranking for help center, periodic batch embedding jobs.
- Observed average QPS during trial: 8 QPS (baseline), peak burst 26 QPS during product event.
- Concurrency observed at peak: ~62 active sessions. Typical concurrency: 18–28.
- Token mix (trial): 60% short calls (<100 tokens payload), 30% medium (100–512), 10% long (>512). Avg tokens per request round-trip: ~520 tokens (input 120 / output 400).
- 75% of calls are chat with history preserved (KV cache hit potential).
- Batch embeddings: 500k rows processed in two runs; embedded throughput sensitivity noted for memory/latency.

Business/ops requirements:
- 99.9% uptime target for in-app chat; p95 latency target <= 350ms for short-turn responses; cost-sensitive (targeting < $0.08 per 1k tokens served on-stable workloads).
- Need audit logs + KMS for keys; retention policy for transcripts (90 days default, 365 for enterprise customers).
- VPC peering mandatory for Dedicated; on-prem not required.

Desired Dedicated sizing (initial request from customer):
- Forecasted go-live traffic (6 months): sustained 40 QPS; 3-hour peak windows up to 85 QPS.
- Concurrency sizing: average concurrent user-sessions 140, peak concurrency 380 (including embeddings bursts).
- Token mix expected similar to trial; plan assumes average tokens per call ~540 after richer templates rolled out.
- Suggested GPU pool: mix of 4 x A100/80GB-equivalent GPUs for model-heavy paths + 8 x 40GB T4-like for smaller reranking/embedding workers; autoscale policy for event-driven spikes.

POC notes and engineering feedback:
- POC observed KV cache reduced costs by ~22% on repeated conversational prompts. Team asked about continuous batching and global routing to fall back to smaller quantized model when demand spikes.
- Concern: cold-start latency for long-context calls; requested guidance on prefix caching and chunking.
- Security review: sent security FAQ (Drive). Legal requested SOC2 Type II report and encryption-at-rest details (KMS flow).

Commercial and next steps:
- AE to provide dedicated sizing worksheet and formal price quote by 2025-02-12. SE to run model mix/quantization recommendation and a quick bench of 2 candidate model variants.
- Plan a 60-min procurement + networking call (networking diagram required) w/ infra + security on 2025-02-19.
- Blockers: VPC IP ranges, SOC2 evidence, final ARR sign-off.

Sales notes (shorthand):

- "We need predictable bills — spikes kill our MRR math" — CFO quote paraphrased.
- Decision driver: price per token + SLA.
